title: An affine open in a smooth integral variety has a Cartier boundary
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X/k$ be a smooth integral separated scheme of finite type [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. For every nonempty affine open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-open-immersion], there is an effective Cartier divisor $D\subseteq X$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] with $|D|=|X|\setminus|U|$. Thus $U=X\setminus|D|$. The empty effective Cartier divisor is permitted.

source.place: Tag 0BCW, divisors-lemma-complement-open-affine-effective-cartier-divisor, applied using smooth regularity (Varieties Tag 056S, varieties-lemma-smooth-regular) and regular local unique factorization (More on Algebra Tag 0AG0, more-algebra-lemma-regular-local-UFD); this is the affine-complement step in groupoids.tex, lemma-algebraic-quasi-projective.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], $X$ is regular and locally Noetherian, since its structure morphism to the field $k$ is smooth. Finite type in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] includes quasi-compactness over the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $X$ is quasi-compact. Thus $X$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact).

source.place: Tag 0BCW, Noetherian hypothesis; Varieties Tag 056S, varieties-lemma-smooth-regular; Properties Tag 01OV, properties-definition-noetherian

proof.text: Put $E=|X|\setminus|U|$. Integrality means irreducibility and reducedness by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Every nonempty open in an irreducible space is dense: otherwise it and the nonempty open complement of its closure would be disjoint, contradicting irreducibility. Hence $U$ is dense. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], write $E=Z_1\cup\cdots\cup Z_r$ with the $Z_i$ its irreducible components, allowing $r=0$. Give each $Z_i$ the reduced induced closed subscheme structure of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], each closed irreducible subset $Z_i\subseteq X$ has a generic point $\xi_i$.

source.place: Tag 0BCW, first sentence of proof; Properties Tag 0BA8, properties-lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components; Schemes Tag 01J4, schemes-definition-reduced-induced-scheme

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-open-boundary-codimension-one] to $X$ and $U$: separatedness is assumed, local Noetherianity was obtained in step 1, affineness is assumed and density was proved in step 2. Thus $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}=1$ for every $i$. The scheme $X$ is integral, regular and locally Noetherian, and $Z_i\hookrightarrow X$ is an integral closed subscheme with that generic-local dimension. Therefore [lem-per-regular-prime-divisor-local-equations] says that its ideal $\mathcal I_i$ is an effective Cartier ideal.

source.place: Tag 0BCW, second and third sentences of proof: Tag 0BCV, divisors-lemma-complement-affine-open; Tag 0AGA, divisors-lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD, in the regular-scheme case

proof.text: Construct the closed subscheme $D$ with ideal $\mathcal I=\mathcal I_1\cdots\mathcal I_r$ by repeated application of [lem-weil-pbc-product-ideal-closed-subscheme-union]; for $r=0$ take the empty closed subscheme with unit ideal $\mathcal O_X$. That statement also gives $|D|=\bigcup_iZ_i=E$, so $X\setminus|D|=U$. Cartier condition: fix $x\in X$. By step 3 and [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] choose affine opens $V_i\ni x$ with $\mathcal I_i(V_i)=f_i\mathcal O_X(V_i)$, $f_i$ a non-zero-divisor. Apply [lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both] $r$ times, using that a principal open of a principal open is principal ($D_{D_V(g)}(a/g^n)=D_V(ag)$): this gives an affine open $W\ni x$ which is a principal open $D_{V_i}(g_i)$ of every $V_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme] (0), $\mathcal O_X(W)=\mathcal O_X(V_i)_{g_i}$, and by quasi-coherence $\mathcal I_i(W)$ is generated by the image of $f_i$. That image is still a non-zero-divisor: if $f_i\,a/g_i^n=0$ then $g_i^mf_ia=0$ for some $m$, so $g_i^ma=0$ and $a/g_i^n=0$. By [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], $\mathcal I(W)=\mathcal I_1(W)\cdots\mathcal I_r(W)=(f_1\cdots f_r)$, and $f_1\cdots f_r$ is a non-zero-divisor of $\mathcal O_X(W)$: if $(f_1\cdots f_r)a=0$, cancel $f_1$, then $f_2$, and so on, obtaining $a=0$. For $r=0$ the generator is $1$. Thus $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].
